Commentary.Commentary: The trophy has been handed over to Shakib as he along with his teammates is posing for photographs. A proud moment for him and his side. They have bounced back brilliantly after being thrashed in the Test series. Windies, on the other hand, will be disappointed in not winning the T20I series, a format in which they are surely amongst the best. Nevertheless, they now have to put all that behind and focus on what is coming up. For now, it is time for us to say goodbye. We have loved your company and wish to see you around next time. Till then, take care.

Bangladesh skipper and Man of the Series, Shakib Al Hasan, says they showed a lot of character, especially after losing the first game. Adds that their confidence has received a boost and he hopes they can kick on. He further mentions he was batting and bowling well throughout and he hopes it continues. States they have been doing really well in the shorter formats and this win will help them perform better against other big teams. Ends by thanking the support that the crowd has given them.

Man of the Match, Liton Das, says he feels really good beating the Windies as they are the T20I World Champions. He reckons the wicket was really good for batting as it was similar to the ones they get at home. He thanks god and feels fortunate for scoring his first fifty in T20Is.

Windies skipper, Carlos Brathwaite, says they could have won the game if they had kept wickets in hand. Credits his bowlers for pulling things back after the start Bangladesh got. Admits Bangladesh played better cricket and congratulates them. Ends by saying Rovman Powell's batting and Ashley Nurse's bowling have been the positives on this tour.

Powell and Ramdin did build a good 45-run partnership but it did not come at a rate which was required. Russell then came out all guns blazing, clearing boundaries at will and evoked belief in the Windies camp but he lacked support from the other end. His blitzkrieg meant the hosts needed 50 from the last three, something which other teams have managed to achieve in the past but his wicket was the final nail in the coffin. He fell prey to the most impressive bowler in this series, Mustafizur Rahman, who finished with another 3-fer before rain intervened once again. The Windies were 19 runs behind from where they had to be at the end of 17.1.

Another clinical performance by them. This time it was set up by their batsmen, Liton Das especially whose 32 ball 61 in the first innings helped his side set a target which was surely above par on this sluggish surface. With runs on the board, their bowlers came out and bowled excellent lines and length. Used all their variations to great effect and had the Windies 3 down with not a lot on the scoreboard in the Powerplay.

So that is it! The customary handshakes happening as the game has been called off and Bangladesh, courtesy the DLS method, have won the game and the series 2-1. Their players are out there and are having a complete ball. A few players performing some dance moves in front of the crowd  while the others soak in the applause from their supporters. They deserve every bit of it as they have come out victorious against all odds.

Well, the rain is back! Bangladesh won't mind though as they are winning according to the DLS method. it is pouring down at the moment. Let us hope it is once again a passing shower and we get the remaining overs in.

OUT! Game, set and match! It has to be, right? Well, looking at the way the Bangladesh players are celebrating, they surely feel so. A low full toss on off, not the easiest of deliveries to put away. Russell does try to hit it over the long off fence but it goes off the lower part of the bat. Ariful Haque there does really well to judge it and takes it just inside the rope with the fingers pointing towards the sky. End of a power-packed innings by Russell, he walks back dejected but he is the reason why the Windies have gotten so close in the first place.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
Clever from Russell. He does not take the single as Nurse gets a thick outside edge towards third man. 14 from this over and they need half of 100 from the last three overs.
Full on off, Russell hits it down to long off for a run.

SIX! Russell continues hitting maximums despite losing partners. Another slower ball on off, Russell this time picks it and once you do that. It is a free hit. He waits for it and then smashes it over the long off fence.
Ashley Nurse strides out to bat.

OUT! Brathwaite holes out! Another failure for him. Excellent change of length by Hider. He bangs it short outside off, Carlos may not have expected it as his weight is on the front foot. He still tries to drag his pull but only gets a top edge which lobs towards long on where the substitute, Sabbir Rahman, cups it by taking a couple of steps backward.
Changes the angle and comes around the wicket. Bowls a slower one and Russell hits it towards deep mid-wicket for a run. Bangladesh will be happy with the fact that he is not on strike.

SIX! This one is colossal! WOW! He is keeping the Windies alive here. This is right in his arc, full and on middle, Russell tonks it over the long on fence. Pressure on the bowler now. They need this to be a huge over, a 20 run over or maybe even more.
In comes Abu Hider for the 17th over.

Brilliant from Rubel Hossain! Just 5 from his last over as he finishes with figures of 4-0-28-1. He bowls it full and wide outside off, CB swings but misses. 64 from 24, the run chase now looks a farfetched one.
Still no boundaries in this over! Full and outside off, Carlos hits it through covers and the batsmen take two.
Another single! Singles won't do for the Windies. Russell clobbers this down to long off for just a run.
Now a dot! Very well bowled! Bowls it wide outside off, Russell maybe not expecting that line and hence lets it be.

The big man tries to be cheeky with a paddle scoop but misses to get hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards square leg and the batsmen run a leg bye. Good start by Rubel, just two singles from the first two.
Well bowled! A yorker one middle, it also tails back in. Russell tries to go big but gets an inside edge through mid-wicket for a run.
Rubel Hossain is back on.

Loopy outside off, eased to covers for nothing. Shakib finishes another good spell. His figures read 4-0-22-1 and Windies need 69 off last 5 overs. Can they do it? Russell surely can! It's a test of nerves now.

Four Byes! Windies won't mind that. The uneven bounce in the pitch comes to the aid of the hosts. Shakib bowls a fuller ball outside off, Russell looks to get bat to it from his crease but the ball scrapes along the track and through the legs of Rahim behind the sticks. The ball races to the fence. So, after 3 singles off the first 4 balls, a boundary results.
Flatter again on the pads, flicked through mid-wicket for an easy single.
Slower on middle, punched to long on for another single.
Carlos has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Flatter around off, pushed to covers for a run.
A surprise short delivery by Rahman. Brathwaite does really well to evade it at the very last moment. 13 from the over. Just the rate they need to go at.
Slower ball on the pads, Carlos tucks it around the corner and some good running gets them two.
Back of a length, surprisingly, Russell plays a defensive stroke towards point for a quick run.

FOUR! How strong is this guy? That has gone to the fence like a tracer bullet. Rahman goes full and outside off, Russell slaps it through covers off balanced, beating the dive of the fielder in the deep for a boundary. He is on a roll here.

SIX! That is out of here! Get the bag of balls out. WOAH! What a hit! Length ball on middle, Russell walks across and hits it way over the long on fence. He is dealing in maximums and Windies would hope he does not stop.
Skipper Carlos Brathwaite is the next man in.

OUT! In the air... taken! Another batsman pays the price for playing across the line. Never a good idea doing so, especially to Rahman who is always angling the ball away from you. He lands it on the shorter side outside off, rolls his fingers over it and slants it away further with the angle. Powell needed to go and hence, he tries to clear the mid-wicket fence with the pull. He only manages to get a top edge which goes high up in the air towards backward point where Hider settles under it and takes it. Half the side back in the hut for the Windies. The good thing for them though is they still have Russell out there.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.

Once again a dot after the biggie. Shakib changes the angle and bowls it from over the wicket. He pitches it outside leg and then gets it to turn into the batsman. Russell does not expect it to turn and shoulders arms but the ball hits him on the pads. No harm done in the end.

SIX! BRUTE! This guy is all about power and that shot is the perfect example. Shakib attacks the stumps and bowls it quicker. Russell clears his front leg and flat-bats it over the long on fence for the second maximum in the over. 89 in 43 needed now.
Quicker on the stumps, Russell keeps it out.
SIX! Russell has come out all guns blazing here. He goes down on one knee and with the angle, slog sweeps it over the mid-wicket fence for his second maximum.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Eases this through long on for a run.
Shakib Al Hasan is back on for the 13th over.

SIX! BANG! Russell has deposited this one into the stands. He says enough is enough as he goes deep into his crease expecting a short one. He gets one and he pulls it with power over the mid-wicket fence. 4,0,W,0,0,6 is how this over reads.
Good change in length by the pacer. He bangs it short and Russell is surprised by it as he ducks under it.
Good length again on middle, Russell tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Andre Russell is the new man in.

OUT! TIMBER! The bowling change has worked for Bangladesh as another one bites the dust. It is a length ball which tails back in a little from outside off. It also skids off the surface. Ramdin clears his front leg and goes for the heave but misses it altogether. The ball clips the off pole. Ramdin starts walking back but he has been asked to wait as the umpire wants to check the front foot. Replays show it is fine and Ramdin is given the marching orders.
A dot to follow the boundary! Good comeback by Rubel, he bowls it slower and outside off. Ramdin tries to go downtown but misses.
FOUR! Starts off with a poor delivery, on the pads. Ramdin is good enough to put that away as he flicks it fine through the leg side. A boundary to begin the over, ideal start for the Windies.
Rubel Hossain is back into the attack.
A couple to end a good over for the Windies. 12 from it. Powell plays this well, he works it through square leg with soft hands and runs two. 112 more needed in 9 overs.
WIDE! A bumper on middle, Powell lets it be and the umpire signals a wide. Rahim is not happy but replays show it was the right call.
A single now as Ramdin pushes it through covers.
Another back of a length delivery on middle, Ramdin guides it to point. So two dots after going for 8 off the first two balls.
Well fielded. Rahman shortens his length on off, Ramdin once again tries to guide it through backward point but the fielder there dives to his left and makes a good stop.

SIX! Boom boom goes Ramdin. Rahman pays the price for bowling a touch too full. Ramdin clears his front leg and lofts it over long on for a biggie. 8 from the first two balls. They need to convert this into a big one.
Nice shot! On the shorter side, it was the cutter by Rahman on off. Ramdin makes room and guides it through backward point for a brace.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
Ramdin flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single. 61 off the first 10 and 124 required off the last 10.

Brilliant effort in the deep from Haque. Bangladesh have been so active in the field in the last couple of matches and they made Windies work hard for their runs. Powell hoicks the fullish delivery to long off. Haque there runs to his left, puts in the dive and keeps them to one. Pressure piling up slowly but surely.
Wide outside off, a touch short as well, Ramdin uses his long lever and punches it towards cover for a run.
Worked through the on side for an easy single.
Ooh! Nice and straight from Shakib. This one comes in with the angle and Powell is late to get his bat down in time and gets an inside edge onto his pads. No harm done in the end.
Shakib bowls a flatter delivery on off to which Ramdin plays the cut and runs a single through the point region.
Shakib Al Hasan comes back.

FOUR! Short and punished. They have managed to turn this into a good over. A shortish ball bowled by Sarkar on middle and off, Powell hacks it across the line and gets it powerfully to the square leg fence on a bounce. 8 runs came off this one.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Half-tracker from Soumya in line of the stumps, Ramdin slogs it across to mid-wicket and changes strike.
Punched through covers for an easy single. So, 3 singles off the first 3 balls. Can they turn this into a big one?
On the pads this time, Ramdin works it to the on side for another run. 50 up for Windies.
Full outside off, driven towards covers for a run.
Cuts the short ball to the point fielder for nothing. The required run-rate is going up and up with every over.
Shows the full face of the bat and gets it to mid-wicket for a single.

Edged but safe! A short of a length ball on off, Powell again slashes hard but the extra bounce means an outside edge is induced. The ball goes aerially towards third man and the fielder there runs in and saves a couple for his team.
FOUR! Slashed and slashed hard. A full ball wide of off stump. Powell throws his bat at it from his crease and manages to get it up and over point. A boundary results.

Hustle from the Windies batters. An angled delivery around off from Hossain, Ramdin manages to get an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls near the stumps. Powell sets off for a run and the striker obliges. A quick single is taken.
Pacy delivery on a back of a length, cut uppishly through backward point for a run.
Rubel Hossain is back on.
On the pads, flicked to mid-wicket for another single.
Slower on a length, pushed towards cover. One run taken.
Wide!  Unusual bounce. Too high to worry the batsman! The umpire has signalled a wide.
Shortish on middle and leg, Ramdin fails to put it away and gets hit on his thigh pad. The ball rolls to the right side of the stumps and the keeper and the bowler make sure that no run is taken.
Rovman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total.
Wrists the length ball to the on side off the back foot for a run.
Wide! Full and down the leg side again. The umpire signals wide.
Fuller around off, driven towards covers for a run.
Denesh Ramdin is the next man in.

OUT! You bet he can. Ends it by shattering the stumps. Yes, the ball did stay low but credit to Shakib for varying his pace beautifully. Bowled the last one a touch slow and on the fuller side. This time he bowls it quicker and on a slightly shorter length. Once again it is the arm ball as it comes in with the angle. Samuels goes back to punch it through the off side but the ball stays very low. Samuels is too late to adjust as the ball goes beneath his bat and hits the middle stump. He stands there in disbelief but then has to walk back. Third wicket in the Powerplay for Bangladesh and they now have the Windies in dire straits. They need another 153.
On the stumps, slower through the air this time. Kept out by Samuels. Just a single so far, can he end it well?
Fires it on the pads, Samuels goes back and tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. The last over of the Powerplay is turning out to be a very good one for the visitors.
This time Powell goes back and whips it through mid-wicket with the angle and gets to the other end.
The arm ball on off, Powell goes back and keeps it out.
Flatter on off, the batsman guides it to point.
Shakib Al Hasan is into the attack.
Shows the full face of the bat and keeps it out. End of another successful over for the visitors.
Wide! Down the leg side, wided.
Rovman Powell walks in next.

OUT! What, really? Walton has hit that down the throat of the substitute fielder Sabbir Rahman at long on. A nothing delivery really, on middle and on a length, Walton lofts it off the front foot but gets more height than distance. An easy catch in the deep and Windies lose a wicket to the part-timer. He is ecstatic and so is the Bangladesh camp.
Wide! The ball is way wide on the leg side but the batsman still goes after it. The umpire signals a wide.
Marlon works it down the leg side. One run added to the total.
Oh no! This is unfortunate. Nazmul Islam has gone out of the field due to the injury on his left hand. Soumya Sarkar will complete his over.

Ouch! This will pain a lot. He bowls a floated delivery in line of the stumps, Samuels pushes it tentatively towards the mid on region. Islam dives to stop the ball to his right. He manages to do so successfully but Walton steps on his right hand while trying to get back in his crease. His fingers start to bleed straightaway and he is walking off the field to get some treatment. Really unfortunate this.
Fuller on off, driven to mid off for another easy run.
Flatter on the pads, worked to the on side for a run.
Nazmul Islam is on.
Short, Walton fails to connect to the pull. End of a successful over for Bangla tigers.
Marlon Samuels is the new man in.

OUT! In the air... gone! Proactive stuff from the visitors. Just a ball prior to this one, Islam was sent to the deep backward point region for this exact shot. Rahman cleverly delivers this wide outside off, angling it across Fletcher. The batsman slices it from his crease. The ball goes aerially towards the fielder who stations himself nicely and takes the catch just inside the fence. Bangladesh have their first after keeping a check on the run-rate.
A wild hoick across the line from Chadwick. He gets it to wide of mid on and changes strike.
Full and wide outside off, Walton fails to connect to the ball.

No backup means FIVE RUNS. Lucky for Windies. Fletcher gently taps the length ball towards the backward point region and sets off for a run. Das there runs in and collects the ball in his stride. He has a shy at the striker's end but misses the stumps. There is no fielder in the mid-wicket region through which the ball goes after missing the sticks. The fielder from deep square leg runs to his left, puts in a dive but fails to stop the ball. Four extra runs.
A play and a miss. A back of a length ball outside off, Andre fails to connect to it.
Mustafizur Rahman is into the attack.

FOUR! Risky but effective! Walton looks set to play the role of the aggressor. He gets a length ball with width on offer. He flashes hard at it from his crease, gets it over cover-point and into the boundary. 8 off the third over.
Fletcher rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. The batsmen have run through for a single.

Uuf! Things happening here. Walton is living dangerously. Hider bowls a length ball outside off, Walton punches it to mid off and sets off for a run. The fielder there runs in, collects the ball and has a shy at the stumps at the bowler's end but misses. The replay shows that Walton would have been gone had the ball hit but it wasn't to be.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.

Almost, almost a wicket. Just short of Sarkar running in from long on. A fuller ball on middle, Walton lofts it in anticipation to clear the fence but the connection wasn't there. The ball lobs towards the mid on region. Sarkar stationed at long on runs in, puts in a dive but still couldn't reach it. A brace results.
Starts this over from around the wicket, angling it into the right-hander. Defended to covers for nothing.
A flash and a miss. Another skiddy delivery from Hossain. Fletcher looks to slash it through the off side but fails. Decent start from both the teams.
Good comeback from Rubel after being hit for a boundary. He bowls a short of a length ball around off which Andre could only defend back to him.
Shortish in line of the stumps, pushed to short mid-wicket for another single.
Walton has driven that ball straight back.
FOUR! Beautiful, Chadwick Walton. Looked so easy. A back of a length delivery on the hips, Walton gets into position and flicks it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Nice pace and bounce from Rubel. A back of a length ball outside off, it skids off the surface and goes past the flashing blade of Walton.
Rubel Hossain to share the new ball.
Shortish on off, pushed to mid off for a run. 7 off the first over.
FOUR! Caressed! Lovely timing on the length ball to get it through covers for the first boundary of the innings.
Short of a length around off, blocked off the back foot.
Leg Bye! Starting a bit too straight again. Again erring in line and bowls it on the pads. Fletcher tries to flick but the ball brushes his pads and rolls to the leg side. A single taken.
Leg Bye! On a length on the pads, Walton fails to put bat to ball and gets hit on the pads. A leg bye stolen.
Starts with a back of a length ball around off, pushed to covers by Chadwick.
We are ready to go. Andre Fletcher and Chadwick Walton is the opening duo for Windies. Abu Hider has the new ball in his hand. Here we go...
